references.text: The Lord struck Pharaoh and his household with great plagues because of Sarai – God intervenes to protect Sarah, just as he does with Abimelech.
Abimelech sees Isaac caressing Rebekah and realizes she is his wife. He warns the people not to touch them – a parallel situation where God protects.
God allowed no one to wrong them; he warned kings on their behalf: "Do not touch my anointed ones, do no harm to my prophets!"
Abigail tells David that the Lord has kept him from bloodguilt – an example of God preventing people from sinning.
David acknowledges that the Lord held him back from doing evil – parallel to how God prevented Abimelech from sinning against Sarah.
God strikes the enemy with blindness to protect his own – an example of God's direct intervention to prevent harm.
Parallel account of God intervening in dreams to prevent sin against His chosen ones.
Contrast between human caution (in the Psalms) and divine protection (in Genesis) to prevent sin.
Parallel about refraining from touching a person under God's protection (God's intervention versus human self-control).
Highlights the theme of God protecting the innocent through human restraint from vengeance.
Theological connection regarding God's relationship with humanity's 'upright heart' and its consequences.
Illustrates that God's protection and presence are linked to a person's upright heart.
Parallel on how a righteous life/upright heart serves as a safeguard against falling.
Theological contrast: God's righteousness in preventing sin (Genesis) versus forgiving sin (Romans).
Highlights God's righteous character acting to prevent injustice against the innocent.
Theological contrast: God's grace in preventing sin (Genesis) vs. forgiving sin (1 John).
Contrast: God's protection from committing injustice (Genesis) vs. God's grace in suffering injustice (1 Peter).
Direct theological connection: God's salvation is directed toward those with a 'sincere heart'.
Direct theological connection: God's righteousness is directed toward those with a 'sincere heart'.
